title: Cross-tenant authorization orchestration checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working doc captures considerations, a concrete checklist, and short query recipes for rolling out the next-generation authorization surface across tenants and downstream SIEM/export pipelines. Focus areas: permissions model changes (role -> capability + attribute), audit schema changes for cross-tenant evidence, evidence automation sampling, and safe rollout/gating when multiple tenants share pipelines.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Preserve tenant isolation in audit exports while enabling centralized detection rules.
- Emit consistent, compact evidence records suitable for SIEM ingestion (low cardinality fields + tenant-aware identifiers).
- Provide staged gating and rollback hooks per-tenant and per-ingress-path.
- Automate evidence sampling and sign-off signal to reduce manual audits.

Open questions (to resolve before canary):
- Do we attach full principal graph for every authorization decision, or just a pointer to a canonical snapshot? cost/size tradeoff.
- How do we represent timebound grants that cross tenant boundaries (support cross-tenant delegation use-cases)?
- Minimum viable SIEM schema: which fields are required vs optional? (see proposed schema below)

Proposed compact audit schema (required fields):
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: iso8601
- tenant_id: string (internal ID)
- tenant_namespace: short human-readable (customer-acct) -- for analytics only
- principal_id: string
- principal_type: user|service|system
- action: canonical_action_id (e.g., resource.read.v2)
- resource_id: string
- resource_type: string
- decision: allow|deny|conditional
- decision_reason: short token (cache_hit|policy_match|fallback|expired_grant)
- policy_snapshot_ref: short-hash (points to stored policy bundle)
- evidence_refs: list-of-ids (optional)

Notes: evidence_refs points to separate evidence blobs stored in EvidenceLake (object store) to avoid huge per-event payloads. The SIEM export adapters should optionally fetch referenced blobs for specific alerts.

Evidence automation: sampling and retention
- Default sampling strategy: 1% of allow events, 100% of deny/conditional events, 100% of escalations and admin actions.
- Tenant opt-in: enterprise tenants can request 100% sampling for a time window via support flow (JIRA SC-xxxx).
- Retention tiers: short (30 days), medium (365 days), archival (7 years) depending on regulatory label.
- Automation hooks: when sampling triggers capture, create an evidence package that includes token traces, policy diff, KV cache snapshot and contextual trace ids. Evidence packages are immutable and checksum-signed.

Cross-tenant SIEM export considerations
- Never emit tenant PII or raw user email. Use tenant-local pseudonyms and tenant-scoped principal_id.
- Add tenant_shard field for export agents so downstream SIEM can isolate alerts without full tenant name.
- Map high-cardinality fields to hashed buckets before export (resource_id hashing with salt per-tenant) when exporting to multi-tenant shared SIEM clusters.
- Enforce export contract: every exported batch must have origin_metadata {origin_cluster, exporter_version, pipeline_run_id}.

Rollout checklist (per-tenant gating)
Phase 0: infra prep (pre-reqs)
- [ ] EvidenceLake storage path and retention policies provisioned (CONFLUENCE-SEC-STORAGE-03)
- [ ] Export adapters updated to new schema (backwards-compatible) with feature flag.
- [ ] SIEM teams allocated staging workspace with hashed buckets enabled.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created: per-tenant decision rate, sampling rate, evidence-trigger rate.

Phase 1: opt-in pilot (3–5 tenants)
- [ ] Feature flag on for pilot tenants only; baseline capture 100% denies + 1% allows.
- [ ] Run daily diff between old-schema exports and new-schema exports (ticket JIRA-SC-4824).
- [ ] Validate SIEM correlation rules against new fields (SOC runbook session).
- [ ] Collect feedback from tenant security admins (weekly 1:1).
- [ ] Verify retention/restore flow for evidence packages.

Phase 2: broaden rollout (20% of tenants)
- [ ] Enable adaptive sampling (increase to 5% allows for tenants with high anomalous rate).
- [ ] Introduce per-tenant emergency rollback (api: /admin/tenant/{id}/authz-v2-rollback).
- [ ] Record SLA metrics: extra latency p50/p95 from policy lookup and evidence packaging.

Phase 3: global default
- [ ] Turn on by default for new tenants; existing tenants get notified and opt-in window closes after 90 days.
- [ ] SIEM exporters default to hashed exports for multi-tenant exports.
- [ ] Run trust audit: sample 100 evidence packages across tenants and reconcile with policy snapshots.

Operational runbook highlights (quick ops bullets)
- If evidence package creation error spikes: toggle off evidence packaging for affected region, open incident runbook INC-AUTH-21.
- If SIEM ingest rejects export: fallback to batched archive + notify SOC; do not retry unmodified until schema compatibility confirmed.
- Rollback process: call admin rollback endpoint -> switch exporter to compatibility mode -> run reconciliation job to backfill missing fields.

Sample SIEM query recipes (Elastic-like pseudo-queries)
- Detect cross-tenant lateral movement:
  index: authz-exports-*, query: "decision:allow AND action:(iam.impersonate OR iam.link-account) AND tenant_shard:[* TO *]"
- High rate of conditional denies per principal:
  query: "principal_id:PRINC_ID AND decision:conditional | stats count() by outcome over 5m"

Backwards compatibility strategy
- New exporter always writes both "legacy_event" and "compact_event" in staging pipelines. Legacy consumers read legacy_event; new consumers read compact_event. After 30 days of parity we retire legacy_event.
- Provide adapter library: exporter-sdk v2 that consumer teams import to avoid bespoke mappers.

Developer checklist for implementers
- [ ] Add policy_snapshot_ref generation (short-hash) at policy compile time.
- [ ] Implement evidence_refs pointer creation and upload to EvidenceLake with id format: EL-{tenant}-{timestamp}-{rand}
- [ ] Implement per-tenant salt management for resource hashing (KMS-protected).
- [ ] Add per-tenant feature flags and the admin rollback endpoint.
- [ ] Unit tests that validate sampling rate boundary conditions.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Schedule SOC tabletop to walk through exports and hashed-bucket workflows (owner: Ethan).
- Spike: cost estimate for storing full-policy blobs vs pointers (Priya).
- Validate export legal checklist for EU tenants (data residency + pseudonymization).

Appendix: example compact_event (as would flow to SIEM; actual export uses newline JSON lines):
{
  "event_id": "f2b9d9a2-8b7e-4a2f-9f61-c1d123a0b9c7",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-15T18:22:43Z",
  "tenant_id": "t-3421",
  "tenant_namespace": "acme-corp",
  "principal_id": "p-9a2f3",
  "principal_type": "service",
  "action": "storage.object.read.v1",
  "resource_type": "object",
  "resource_id_hash": "h:0f3b...",
  "decision": "allow",
  "decision_reason": "policy_match",
  "policy_snapshot_ref": "ps:7c9d",
  "evidence_refs": []
}

(End of note)

-- Maya
